# 📋 OPEN-ITEMS — the single registry (W0)

**The one place deferred/open work lives.** Created by W0 (PRODUCTION_PLAN §W0) because closure state
was scattered across four docs with drift — which is exactly how "all boxes checked" and "not
production-ready" were both true. **Updating this file is part of the "Gate before done" checklist**
(CLAUDE.md): when your change closes, opens, or retires an item, sweep it here in the same PR.

Severity: **blocker** (ship-stopper on its surface) · **high** (real security/money/ops gap) ·
**med** (correctness/a11y with a plausible trigger) · **low** (hardening/polish) · **config** (needs
Min, not code); a struck severity (~~high~~) marks a retracted row. Status: **open** (a leading
⚑ partial says what shipped and what is left) · **planned:Wx** (owned by a W-track phase) · **gated**
(external prerequisite) · **parked:A1** (the surface the row guards is switched OFF in `apps/qr/lib/surfaces.ts`
— drawn nowhere, refused at its actions — so the defect is unreachable; the row stays IN PLACE with
its text, and flipping the constant back reopens it unchanged: reopen the rows in the same PR as the
surface) · **accepted risk** (kept on purpose, with its revisit condition) · **closed** / **done** /
**retired** (with the closing PR). A row's next step, when it has one, is the Item's closing
**Next:** sentence — the Status cell holds only a status. Closed items move to the Closed section with
the closing PR — don't delete rows. Counts of open or closed rows are never written here: count them
from the Status cells, e.g.

```bash
node -e 'let h,c={};for(const l of require("fs").readFileSync("docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md","utf8").split("\n")){if(!l.startsWith("|")){h=null;continue}const x=l.replace(/\\\|/g,"").split("|").slice(1,-1).map(s=>s.trim());if(!h){h=x;continue}const i=h.indexOf("Status");if(i<0||/^-+$/.test(x[0]))continue;const v=x[i].replace(/[*_]/g,"").trim();const s=/^✅/.test(v)?"closed":(v.replace(/^⚑\s*/,"").split(/[ (:·—]/)[0]||"?").toLowerCase();c[s]=(c[s]||0)+1}console.log(c)'
```

rows (settle 43 · split 35) guard those barely-used doors. So: subtract. The brief is the artifact

| M210 | **high** | **Owner 2026-10-07 ([#5](OWNER_RULINGS_2026-10-07.md)): team-safety migration go.** **Two owners demoting each other concurrently can leave the restaurant with NO owner.** Codex round 4 P1 on #278. Both requests pass their non-self checks, both refresh while both callers are still owners, and each updates a different target row guarded only by that target's own old role — so both writes succeed. Nobody is left who can restore ownership and recovery is a manual database update. The statement-level guard cannot express this: the invariant is over the TABLE (at least one active owner), not the row being written. A TypeScript owner-count before the write would be two statements again — it would stop the accidental case while leaving the raced one, which is worse than not claiming a fix. Needs the invariant enforced atomically in the database, i.e. a prod migration, applied as ONE file through the Supabase MCP `apply_migration` once its PR is green, at a quiet time the owner names (ruling #5, with M208 and M205; never `db push` — M125). | M41  | low      | **A failed reward apply/remove whose write actually LANDED drops focus to `<body>`.** `RewardField`'s failure-path focus claim is consumed by the first idle commit; if the throw's write did land and the follow-up re-read then succeeds, the branch swaps a commit LATER and the node the claim captured is detached (`.focus()` on a detached node is a silent no-op). Narrow — it needs the outage to clear between the two calls — and the claim deliberately cannot outlive that commit, because both cleverer schemes tried here were wrong in the other direction (a commit budget left a unit armed for a peer's realtime flip to steal focus with; tying it to the re-read's promise disarmed it a microtask before React flushed the swap). Real fix = let the parent tell the child that ITS re-read caused the flip, e.g. a monotonically-increasing `changeSeq` prop the child can compare. Before payment the lines are thin too: `TableLineView` (`floor-types.ts:65-84`) carries no modifiers at all (zero `modifiers` hits across floor.ts, floor-types.ts, FloorDetailLive.tsx, StaffLineEditor.tsx), drops the kitchen note on every fired line, and names the line state in hardcoded English. **Fix, no migration, read-and-render:** when the open-cart read is null and a paid/refunded order exists, source the lines from `qr_order_items` using `TRACK_ORDER_SELECT`'s line body (never a fourth select), map into the SAME `TableLineView` with a `settled: true` discriminant so the header reads "Ordered" not "Order so far", and gate the empty branch (`FloorDetailLive.tsx:419`) on `!settled`. Amounts stay verbatim snapshots — never re-derive, never route through `LiveMoney`. | K34                   | med      | **Owner 2026-10-07 ([#5](OWNER_RULINGS_2026-10-07.md)): migration go after K30, at a time the owner names.** **`pickup_config.tz` is text with no CHECK and no validating writer, and the two halves of "today" disagree on a value only Postgres accepts.** Codex round 1 on #281 (P2), verified. `mms_kds_stats()` derives its day in SQL from the stored value, and Postgres's `at time zone` takes names ICU refuses (`'PST'` is a fixed −08:00 there; `'EST5EDT'` too), while the TS side (`resolveServiceTz`) falls back to `America/Los_Angeles` and logs it — so on such a value the served rail floors at LA midnight (07:00Z in summer) and the Avg cell beside it at 08:00Z, one hour apart. No TS writer exists to validate at (the value is set in SQL), so the fix is storage-time: a trigger on `pickup_config` refusing any `tz` not in `pg_timezone_names` (prod migration, one file, Min's go) — or `mms_kds_stats(p_tz)` taking the TS-validated zone so both halves derive from one effective zone. The handled signals (INT/TERM/HUP) restore; locally, after a hard kill, `git status --short` names the module left mutated — read `git diff -- <file>` first and restore it with `git checkout -- <file>` only when the diff is exactly one mutant (CLAUDE.md, Commands). In CI the checkout is discarded. ② The baseline runs the selected suites TOGETHER, and each mutant runs its suite ALONE. A suite that passes only in company would make its mutants CAUGHT for the wrong reason; vitest isolates module scope per file, not filesystem/env. To settle it, run every suite alone once and compare. ③ A mutant that throws at runtime (an undeclared identifier the syntax check accepts) counts as a catch without exercising its rule. Settle with a typecheck of mutated text, or an audit of the replace strings. A fourth class went live once and is closed: a suite whose read depended on render timing scored one mutant SURVIVED on main and CAUGHT on the PR runs of the same files (T52, #324). | ✅  | **M152** — ✅ **DONE (2026-09-05, pilot P0) — all three mouths, plus (c′) from the blind pass: the decline webhook no longer releases the pay-window lock.** A declined intent is still confirmable from the mounted Element, so the cart it prices stays frozen until the diner ends the attempt ("Edit order" cancels it at Stripe and releases lock, pin and link together) or the TTL lets a successor supersede it; the cart-wide release had left a link with no lock (every promo refused as "locked" on an editable cart) and, pre-link, the M151 overlap through the decline door. The one cost: a diner who lost the attempt token (a 3DS decline returns through a full redirect) waits ≤5 min before EDITING; Pay stays live throughout. (a) `applyPromo`'s code write carries `.is("live_payment_intent_id", null)` in the SAME statement (mutant + suite; the diagnosis read knows the link too). (b)/(c) `mms_release_promo_grant` carries `and live_payment_intent_id is null` — the RPC both the stale-grant release and the outer catch call — and `mms_mark_settle_canceled` clears pin AND link only for ITS intent (SQL test `m151_live_payment_intent_test.sql`, 6 cases incl. the legitimate path and the successor-untouched case). The `payment_intent.canceled` webhook gained a single-pay arm keyed on the intent id (`releaseByIntent`). Was: **A promo pin can be cleared while a CAPTURED PaymentIntent still depends on it — the M70 invariant violated from two directions, both live today.** Found while verifying M123/M124 (2026-09-01), each confirmed against source. M70's header states the rule: _"The pin has to outlive the lock for the charge to reconcile at all."_ Stripe retries a webhook up to three times at an 80s timeout, so a capture whose fulfilment lands after `CART_LOCK_TTL_MS` (5 min) must still re-derive WITH the pin. Two paths break that. **(a) `applyPromo` (`lib/cart.ts`)** nulls `promo_granted_cents` in the same statement as the code write, under a freeze predicate that is deliberately TTL-aware (`locked.eq.false,locked_at.is.null,locked_at.lte.${lockCutoff}`) — so five minutes after a diner walks away with a captured intent, a tablemate entering any code nulls the pin that capture reconciles against. **(b) `create-intent`'s stale-grant release** clears the predecessor's pin under the era the successor just stamped; if the predecessor's intent captured and its webhook is merely delayed past the TTL, the takeover legitimately owns the lock and the release legitimately matches — and the reconcile then disagrees with a charged card. Both are the same missing fact and the same fix as **M151**: a cart→intent link, so every pin-clearer can carry `and live_payment_intent_id is null`. Fix all three together. **(c) ADDED 2026-09-01 (#245), found while fixing M153.** `create-intent`'s OUTER CATCH is a third mouth: it fires on a throw from ANYWHERE in the try, including from ABOVE the pin block (an availability read, a pickup RPC), and by then any pin on the row belongs to a PREDECESSOR — so it clears a pin whose PaymentIntent may have captured with a merely-delayed webhook. `mms_release_promo_grant`'s predicate reaches it under BOTH arms (our era matches because we hold the lock; and `locked_at is null` matches if a cart-wide release got there first). Unchanged from `main` — #245 deliberately did not narrow it, because a `pinned` flag would put a money rule in `app/api/**`, outside MONEY_PATHS and outside `verify:slice`'s mutant set, where it could not be guarded at all. Same fix as (a) and (b): the predicate has to be able to say `and live_payment_intent_id is null`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | pilot P0                                                                                                                 |
| ✅  | **M151** — ✅ **DONE (2026-09-05, pilot P0) — merged `dfcda72`, prod row `20260905103039` applied and verified before the merge.** `qr_carts.live_payment_intent_id` names the ONE single-pay intent that may still reconcile against the pin. `create-intent` now makes the predecessor UNUSABLE before anything else — `supersedeCartIntent` retrieves, cancels a cancelable intent, REFUSES (409) on `succeeded`/`processing`, refuses without touching the row (503) when Stripe cannot say — and only then releases the stale grant; the era rides in the Stripe idempotency key so a cancelled intent is never replayed; the link is written after the mint under the minting era and a zero-row write cancels the just-minted intent and 409s. The verdict is a pure module (`lib/live-intent.ts`, 4 mutants), the sequence is `lib/supersede.ts` (3 mutants), rule 3 of `check-promo-grant-pin` pins supersede-before-release as awaited sequencing (red-first on the reorder AND the `Promise.all` shape). Was: **Two concurrent create-intents by the SAME diner can now hold DIFFERENT promo pins, and the older intent is still chargeable.** Found by Codex round 3 on #240 (2026-08-29), verified against source, and it is a NARROW REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THAT PR — not a pre-existing quirk, which is why it is filed high rather than as polish. #240 moved the promo-pin release out of the decline webhook into `create-intent`, where the new attempt clears the previous pin under the era it just acquired and re-derives. `acquireCartLock` deliberately lets the SAME payer re-acquire (`route.ts` §lock: "the SAME payer re-acquiring (refresh / retry) succeeds"), and nothing serializes two overlapping requests — `withinMutationRate` is a rate limit, not a mutex. So request A can mint a PaymentIntent under pin_A while request B re-acquires, clears pin_A and pins pin_B; A is never cancelled. If the promo expires, is disabled, or loses its minimum-subtotal qualification between the two, confirming A charges A's amount while fulfillment re-derives against pin_B — the reconcile mismatch that reads as CHARGED GUEST, NO ORDER. **What it trades against:** BEFORE #240 the second attempt's `mms_pin_promo_grant` no-op'd on the non-null pin, so both intents shared ONE pin and stayed consistent — concurrency was safe, and the SEQUENTIAL re-checkout (decline → edit basket → pay) was the broken case, which is the far more reachable #233 P1 that #240 fixed. This window needs two overlapping requests AND a promo state change between them. Net strongly positive, but not a clean win, and the new failure is worse per occurrence. **Neither remedy is small, which is why this is filed rather than patched:** (a) SERIALIZE same-diner create-intents — cuts against `acquireCartLock`'s deliberate re-acquire, which exists so a diner can re-checkout with a different tip; (b) MAKE THE PREDECESSOR UNUSABLE before replacing its pin — the right shape, and it also settles the inline-retry question #240 wrestled with, but there is NO cart→intent link today (`stripe_payment_intent_id` lives on `qr_orders`, post-fulfillment), so it needs a `qr_carts.live_payment_intent_id` column plus a cancel-on-supersede: a prod migration on a history this repo can only advance one file at a time via MCP. Do (b). Until then the pin is correct for every SEQUENTIAL attempt and wrong only for overlapping ones.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | dfcda72                                                                                                                  |

| ✅  | **T20** — ✅ **DONE (2026-09-03, PR #249) — and the row understated it in two ways a scout pass measured.** **(1) `settling` decays exactly like `locked`** — `assertCartMember` computes both by arithmetic (`locked_at > now - CART_LOCK_TTL_MS`; `settle_at > now - SETTLE_TTL_MS`), so `frozen = locked or settling` has TWO stale-true axes, not one, and the settle window is twice as long at 10 minutes. The row named only the lock. **(2) The lock also removes the ESCAPE ROUTES**, which is what made the dead end permanent rather than merely annoying: `TableTimeline`'s `quiet` drops both /cart links under a freeze, `AppHeader` hides its cart link on /menu, and `CartBar` renders nothing at count 0 — so a diner with a stale lock loses the route to the one surface that does a fresh read. Filed separately as **T22**. **The fix, in three parts.** `CART_LOCK_TTL_MS` and `SETTLE_TTL_MS` moved to `apps/qr/lib/lock-ttl.ts` (no `server-only`), with all seven production importers and three test stubs repointed and NO re-export left behind — two import paths for one value is the shape the name-it-ONCE rule exists to prevent. `freezeRecheckDelayMs` is the new rule and it is the LONGEST held axis, because a cart that is both stays frozen until both lapse; it answers null for an editable cart, which is what keeps this a scheduled re-read rather than a poll. Both arms carry a mutant. ⚠️ **The client cannot compute the expiry and does not try**: `getCartView` returns `locked` and `settling` but never `locked_at` or `settle_at`, so the schedule bounds our IGNORANCE — a freeze observed now was acquired at or before now, so it cannot outlive now + its TTL. ⚠️ **The effect was wrong in BOTH directions before it was right, and each was caught by a different pass.** The first draft fired exactly ONCE — caught in the author's own adversarial read: its deps were the freeze axes, so a re-read finding the cart still frozen changed nothing React could see and no new timer was scheduled, and a second checkout would have held the surface dead for its whole window. The tick that fixed that then never STOPPED — caught as a CRITICAL by the blind adversarial pass: once the table pays, `mms_fulfill_order` sets `qr_carts.status='paid'`, `assertCartMember` throws `cart_closed` BEFORE it computes either freeze axis, and the swallow means `locked` can never fall, so an abandoned tab fired a Server Action every five minutes forever (same shape for a persistent 503, a dead session, an offline tab). The shipped form is a self-arming chain that re-arms **only on a read that came back**: `readView` reports whether it succeeded, a still-frozen SUCCESSFUL read is a re-acquired lock and earns a new window, and a failed read ends the chain — leaving the surface exactly where it was before this change (stale until the next realtime event or foreground), which is the honest floor and is bounded. **And the ownership half:** all four sites inferred `lockedByYou` by comparing against `lockedByName`, which is peer-supplied presence text — a tablemate named "You" made their lock read as the viewer's own, telling an uninvolved diner they were checking out AND suppressing the real holder's name. The correct seat-id derivation already existed in the provider and was simply never exported; `lockedByYou` now is, and `AddButton`, `ItemSheet`, `GuestList` and the provider's own announcer all read the fact instead of the label. Zero `lockedByName === "You"` comparisons remain. ⚠️ **That fixed the FACT and left the SENTENCE**, which the blind pass caught: the peer branch still rendered the raw name, so the same impostor produced **"You is checking out — the order’s locked for a moment"** — ungrammatical, and still opening with the word the attack is built on. `apps/qr/lib/peer-name.ts` narrows a peer name that would read as the reader (letters-only-normalized `you` / `youre` / `u` / `me` / `i`) to the "Someone" the banner already shows for an unresolved seat, applied ONCE at the derivation so the banner and the live region cannot disagree; tested, and carrying two mutants (the impostor hole and the non-Latin erasure the first fix caused). ⚠️ It stops at the SENTENCE: Codex round 4 rejected extending it to the guest-list avatar labels, because a list entry asserts nothing about the reader and the viewer's own row already carries "(you)", so narrowing there only costs a guest called "U" (a Burmese honorific) their identity where a screen-reader user hears it. | #249                                                                                                                     |

MEASURED ON PROD, not inferred from the repo: `pg_get_functiondef` on `public.mms_merge_table_orders` contains both predicates and the chargeable filter. ⚠️ **THE SHAPE, which is why this row keeps its text — and the first draft of this closure got the mechanism wrong too, so these numbers are measured:** **14** migration files redefine this one function (a bare `grep -l` returns 15; `20260823000000_m100_mode_authority.sql` mentions it without redefining it). The S6 fold was NOT added by `m98`, whose own comment says it added the PRICE match. Its real history is **add → drop → restore**: introduced `20260622090000_s2_audit_fixes.sql`, **absent from the next three definers** — including `20260623030000_s3_secure_merge_guard.sql`, the file this row cites, where the defect was GENUINELY LIVE — and restored by `20260702000000_merge_void_guard_restore.sql`, carried ever since. | M218 | **high** | ✅ **CLOSED (2026-09-16) — `mms_refund_cash_line` records it, the drawer nets it, and a SQL test proves it against a real database.** **A cash refund is told, never recorded — the drawer's money out leaves the receipt "Paid in full" and the takings whole.** Codex round 1 on #283 (P1), verified against source: `mms_refund_authorize` (`20260624030000_s4_money_remediation.sql`) answers `split_unsupported` for any order with no PaymentIntent — and `mms_fulfill_cash_order` never writes one — so `refundLine` cannot record a cash refund, and nothing else writes `mms_refunds` / `qr_orders.refunded_cents` / `qr_order_items.refunded_cents` for cash (there is no processor webhook to reconcile it later either). The settled list's cash note (`floor.settled.path.cash`) now says so in both tongues — "hand it back from the drawer; this screen can't record a cash refund yet, so the receipt and the takings still show it as paid" — instead of reading as if the hand-back were logged. M183 closed the mislabel (cash was sent to the card dashboard), not this. Fix = a migration (prod, Min's go): `mms_refund_cash_line(p_line_item, p_initiator)` beside the card authorizer — same manager authority, same per-line pool clamp, the ledger row with a null intent and `tender = 'cash'`, `refunded_cents` on the order and the line, the audit row — then the sheet offers Refund on the cash path and records it, `getDayCashSummary` nets the drawer's refunds, and the receipt's rows carry the movement. A SQL test in `supabase/tests/` asserting the ledger row, the two `refunded_cents` and that a card line still refuses this path. The fix is structural: M126's ambient makes the page grid a **groove** rather than a ridge. A light hairline on a dark ground LIGHTENS the pixel under light text; a dark groove darkens it, so the grid now BUYS contrast instead of spending it. not RENDERED SURFACES** — which is exactly the gap that guard was written to close. Anything that releases that freeze in between (any acquire/release pair on the cart) leaves the share intent confirmable with NO settlement mutex, and `extendSettlement`'s `.gt("settle_at", cutoff)` (`lock.ts:272`) no-ops on the resulting null instead of reporting, so the route returns a client secret and nothing anywhere notices. ⚠️ **PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by #275:** `main`'s `settleCash` already acquires at `staff-cart.ts:260` and releases at `:461`, which is the same window; #275's `standDown` probe and the reverted post-claim releases were further instances of one class, and rounds 12/13/14 each found a different one. The root fix is in the SHARE path, not in `supersede.ts`: `extendSettlement` must report when it extends nothing, and the route must refuse rather than return a secret — or claim its own freeze atomically before minting. Related but distinct from M201 (which is about WHO owns a freeze; this is about a writer riding one it does not own). No migration. | P2e  | med      | ⚠️ **CLOSED WITH ONE EXCEPTION, and the exception is P3b (pilot P3, 2026-09-05).** The remove ships — but a cart carrying a STALE `live_payment_intent_id` refuses it for the life of that cart, so P2e is still reachable there. Traced at the pre-merge blind pass: every writer that nulls the column is event-driven and none is a timer — Stripe's `payment_intent.canceled`, `mms_mark_settle_canceled` (needs a settle that exists), and `supersedeCartIntent` / `releasePayAttemptSafely`, both routed through `readLiveIntentFor(cartId, uid, era)` and therefore reachable ONLY by the diner who minted the intent, on the `locked_at` era that minted it. A guest who opens Checkout, mints an intent and abandons the tab (an iOS app-switch drops the release beacon) leaves a cart where both staff promo doors match zero rows, `refusedPromoReason` answers `locked`, and the register reads "Someone's paying — wait for that to finish" about a payment that is dead — while `canWrite` (TTL-only, link-blind: `floor.ts:344-347`) renders the controls enabled and `mergeTables` still refuses on `promo_code`, pointing at the remove that is itself refused. The predicate is NOT new and must not be loosened: `main` already carries it on the diner door (`git show 5715781:apps/qr/lib/cart.ts` line 459) and it is M151's invariant. **P3b closes this** — a terminal/abandoned intent recorded and released on the cart fixes every gate at once. Not measured, and deliberately not asserted either way: whether Stripe eventually cancels an abandoned never-confirmed PaymentIntent and delivers `payment_intent.canceled`, which would bound the window rather than leave it open forever. Everything else P2e asked for shipped: `apps/qr/lib/staff-promo.ts` ships `clearPromoForTable` — staff-gated, session-addressed, carrying `applyPromo`'s five predicates (status · the TTL-aware pay lock · the TTL-aware settlement freeze · `.is("live_payment_intent_id", null)`), nulling `promo_granted_cents` in the SAME payload (`mms_promo_discount` returns the pin VERBATIM when non-null, so a code-only clear would leave a discount nothing on any surface can explain), and taking the row count from `{ count: "exact" }` — **not** `.select("id")`, which PostgREST 14 re-projects against the top-level `or()` and 42703s (`lock.ts:66-73`). The link gate is on the REMOVE for a sharper reason than on the apply: dropping a code RAISES the total the webhook re-derives. The control lives on the table drill-down (`components/staff/StaffPromoControl.tsx`), so the merge refusal now names an action reachable on the same screen — and `lib/floor.ts`'s sentence was rewritten to say WHICH table carries the code, its comment no longer justifying the absence of a remove. Deliberately NOT an auto-clear: silently dropping a quoted discount is the outcome that comment refuses. Guarded by the `staff-promo/clear-*` and `floor/merge-*` mutants plus `lib/staff-promo.test.ts` and `lib/floor-merge-promo.test.ts`. Was: **A promo code can never be REMOVED, and the floor tells staff to remove it.** Measured at `fb7e095`: `apps/qr/lib/cart.ts` was the ONLY writer of `qr_carts.promo_code` and only ever wrote a non-empty code, while `apps/qr/lib/floor.ts` refused a table merge with "One of these tables has a promo code applied — remove it before merging." — naming an action the product did not implement, so that merge was refused permanently. | P2k  | high     | ✅ **CLOSED (2026-09-24, Phase 2a · send) — the console sends.** `lib/staff-send.ts` (`staffFireCart` moved out of `kitchen.ts`, a coded refusal union, its batch and deadline, `staffUndoFire`) + `useStaffSend` / `StaffSendButton` on the table page: "Send to kitchen · N items" with the diner's server-clocked 10s Undo (`lib/send-grace.ts`), unsent dishes tagged "Not sent", and `cart.ts`'s false docblock claim gone with the move. **Two halves ride later slices:** send-kitchen commit B (the settle gate — a settle that would fire unsent dishes steers to the Send) ships in **2c**, and counter-order sending before payment is **2f** (P2v) — until then the console refuses a counter send. ✅ **Commit B SHIPPED (2026-09-25, Phase 2c · gate)** — every settle door refuses while dine-in dishes are unsent (`staffSettleBlockedByUnsent`), so no P2k-c row is filed. ⚑ **RE-RATED high (2026-09-23 staff UX audit)** — it is not dead code, it is the missing half of a flow: a no-phone "Start a table" order reaches the kitchen only at settle (fire-at-checkout), so a table that pays after eating is never cooked for from the console. Wire it as a "Send to kitchen (N)" on the table page with the diner's grace undo. Was: **`staffFireCart` is an exported Server Action with no caller, and a comment promises the capability it does not deliver.** Measured 2026-09-05: `grep -rn staffFireCart apps/qr` returns exactly two hits — its own definition at `apps/qr/lib/kitchen.ts:400`, and `apps/qr/lib/cart.ts:251`, whose docblock tells the next reader _"staff can always fire from the console via staffFireCart"_. No component or route invokes it. The console's real fire control is `fireTicketNow` (a HELD ticket fired early from the KDS), which is a different capability: it cannot send an unsent cart's lines to the kitchen. So the comment names a staff escape hatch that does not exist, which is exactly the class of claim `docs/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md` calls a promise the code does not keep. Either wire a control or delete both the action and the sentence — the action carries a `staffGate` and a Zod schema, so it is not free to leave lying around. | P2p  | low      | **✅ DONE (2026-09-20, the lane slice)** — the objection was right and the answer is a SHAPE: `lib/expo-errors.ts` takes the subject as `{kind:"table", id}` / `{kind:"bag", x}` / `{kind:"verify", x}`, so a table's number rides `expo.err.bagTable`'s Latin-always `{id}` and a name or code rides `{x}`; `setTogoStatus` carries a code; the region renders `<MsgText>` (a key arrives marked, a sentence through `OutageText`). **The expo bump's two `catch` sentences are frozen English, and the obvious conversion is WRONG — that is why they are filed rather than converted.** `apps/qr/components/staff/ExpoBoard.tsx` raises `Couldn't update {verifyWho} — try again.` / `Couldn't update the bag for {callOut} — try again.` from the bump's `catch`, and the site reads as converted because the render goes through `<OutageText>`. Two things block the one-line fix, both measured. ① `<OutageText>`'s passthrough arm returns `<>{error}</>` — a BARE TEXT NODE (`components/staff/Chrome.tsx`), so a Burmese sentence would land with no `lang` mark: Latin face, Latin leading, announced as English, which is the exact defect rule 5 exists for. ② The `{x}` such a sentence needs is itself bilingual — `callOutAria` is `စားပွဲ 7` — and `<Chrome>`'s slot rule wraps any value containing a Latin character whole in `lang="en"`, so it would mark the Burmese word as English. The real fix is the `Notice` shape `RegisterStart.tsx` already uses (`{kind:"local", k, vars} \| {kind:"server", error}`) plus a table/non-table key per stage, so every slot value is purely Latin — four keys, one discriminated state. Was: **One Server Action that never settles holds EVERY later one on the tab.** Next 16.2.9 (`next/dist/client/components/app-router-instance.js` `dispatchAction` / `runRemainingActions`; `next/dist/client/app-call-server.js`): client Server Actions and `router.refresh()` share one queue; a non-navigation action is appended behind the pending one and not SENT until it settles; only a navigation discards the pending one. A client `raceTimeout` neither cancels the hung action nor frees the queue, so every later write — the pad's sends, a cash settle, a reader settle, a language pick — waits unsent, times out ITSELF on the client while still queued, and is SENT LATER when the hung one settles. Audit each staff client timeout (`useStaffSend`, `usePadWrites`, `CashSettleButton`, `TerminalSettle`, `CloseSecureTabButton` …) for "reported lost, still queued, will still go": idempotency keys should make each safe — verify each, and check the copy ("didn't go through" would be false). The language chain answers its own case (review C1). Read from Next's source, not browser-observed. ⚑ **Measured 2026-10-01 (same probe):** a second action — in its own transition OR a plain `await` — dispatched while one hangs is not answered until the hung one answers, then both land at once. | M108 | med      | **Two session-mode reads fail OPEN, and a third one next to them fails closed.** Found by the M100 mapping pass. `addItem` (`cart.ts:53-64`) and `reorderOrder` (`reorder.ts:118-124`) both do `const { data: sess } = await db.from("table_sessions").select("mode")…` — the error is DISCARDED, so an unreadable session yields `sess === null`, `dineIn === false`, and a **`togo` tag on a dine-in table**. `staff-open-cart.ts:14-22` reads the same column and returns `unavailable: true` instead, which is the W10b shape ("unknowable ≠ X"). The harm is the M100 defect's mirror: a dine-in cold line tagged `togo` is never taxed, so the restaurant UNDER-collects — the direction m97's header calls the worse one legally — and the line stops firing on "Send to kitchen" (`mms_fire_cart` matches `fulfillment = 'dinein'`), so a seated diner's food waits for checkout and picks up a "Bag it" chip and an expo ticket for a plate that never leaves. M100 does not close it: the SQL guard bounds the TOGGLE, and this is the INSERT path. The clean fix is not error handling but deleting the second read — `assertCartMember` already selects from `table_sessions` one call earlier and throws `UNAVAILABLE` if THAT read fails, so returning `mode` from it is the "name it ONCE" rule and removes a round-trip from every add. **CLOSED (#226, 2026-08-23)** — the fix was the deletion, as predicted: `assertCartMember` now selects `mode` on the row it ALREADY reads to prove the session active and returns it on `CartAuthz`, so both call sites read one binding and the second round-trip is gone from every add. The read that remains fails closed (503) — an unreadable session can no longer decide a tax fork. Guarded red-first by a new `lib/cart-add-mode.test.ts` (a `cold_food` fixture, the only shape whose two arms differ, with the expected cents computed by the real `lineTax`) plus the `cart/add-mode-fork-collapses-to-togo` mutant; `reorder-mode.test.ts`'s DB mock now carries NO `table_sessions` row, so re-introducing either second read turns it red. | M109 | med      | **`mms_merge_table_orders` has no SQL session-mode check — the same-mode rule is TypeScript-only.** Found by M100's adversarial pass, which is fitting: it is M100's exact defect shape one function over. The merge re-parents a source cart's lines into a target cart keeping `fulfillment` VERBATIM, and its body contains no reference to `mode` at all (measured against the live function: `prosrc` does not mention it). The rule that a pickup table cannot be merged into a dine-in one lives at `floor.ts:666-667` — _"Only tables of the same kind can be merged."_ — a client-side check in front of a service_role RPC. Materiality is BELOW M100's and that is why it is filed rather than folded in: `mergeTables` is staff-gated and service-role-only, so it is not a public POST a diner can forge, and M97's fold predicate already refuses to merge lines whose tags differ. What it costs is the same thing M100 cost — the invariant is asserted in one place and enforced in another, so the day a second caller appears (a manager tool, a reconciler, a staff surface that merges without going through `floor.ts`) the tags cross modes with nothing to stop them. The fix is the shape already used three times in this schema: join `table_sessions` for both carts inside the write and require the modes equal. **CLOSED (2026-08-23)** — `20260827000000_m109_merge_matches_mode.sql` restates the function (its FOURTEENTH definition) with the rule as a whole-merge GATE, not a fold predicate: two tables of different kinds must not merge at all, so it raises and rolls back beside the existing `both carts open and their tables active` and `no secured tab` gates. The registry's own suggested shape — "inside the write" — was deliberately not taken: a mode term on the delete/re-parent would make a cross-mode merge silently move NOTHING while still cancelling the source cart and closing its session, which is worse than the defect. What the fold predicate bought (M97 refusing to fold mismatched tags) was never the protection it looked like: a refused fold RE-PARENTS, so the line landed on the target cart anyway. `supabase/tests/m109_merge_matches_mode_test.sql` (7 cases) + 7 mutants in `verify-mode-authority.mjs`; measured red-first against the pre-M109 body. **⚠️ The suite shipped for review with FIVE cases and a hole the blind adversarial pass found (HIGH), reproduced directly: a session's `mode` and its lines' `fulfillment` tags travel together in ordinary data, so all five fixtures left the two PERFECTLY CORRELATED — and the suite was measured GREEN against a gate that never read `mode` at all, comparing line tags instead. That is M109's own defect, reintroduced with every test passing.** Cases 4 and 5 break the correlation in opposite directions, which is only possible because it is not a law: a seated diner can tap "To go", so a `dinein` session legitimately holds a `togo` line. Case 4 holds the modes EQUAL while the tags DIFFER (a tag-reading gate refuses; the merge must succeed); case 5 holds the modes DIFFERENT while the tags MATCH (a tag-reading gate allows; the merge must refuse). Both are needed — a gate ANDing a tag conjunct onto a real mode comparison passes 4 and is caught only by 5. The other load-bearing pair: 3 kills the `dinein`-flavoured gate copied from M100 (which passes 1 and 2 while merging scan-and-go into pickup), 7 kills the over-tightening to "both must be dine-in" (which passes 1-6). The same pass also showed the post-refusal assertions cannot prove the gate PRECEDES the destructive tail — a plpgsql `begin … exception` block is an implicit savepoint, so the merge rolls back wherever the gate sits (measured: relocating it below `update table_sessions set status = 'closed'` leaves the file green). They are now labelled as the fixture-drift checks they are. `floor.ts` maps the new raise to its own sentence rather than the generic "a table changed", which the change would otherwise have made | M46  | low      | ✅ **DONE — M46 (2026-09-04, PR #252): the DECISION this row asked for, made both ways.** It asked to "either add a jsdom project to the vitest config for component tests, or write down the rule that decision logic never lives in a `.tsx`" — and the honest answer was both. `apps/qr/vitest.config.ts` now includes `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, and a component suite opts into a DOM **one file at a time** with `/** @vitest-environment jsdom */`, which vitest reads out of raw file text and prefers over the config. ⚠️ **NOT `test.projects`** — measured and rejected: with `extends: true` a child's `include` CONCATENATES with the parent's, so a jsdom project silently re-runs every node suite under jsdom (node 1274, dom 1275), and without `extends` the alias and the JSX runtime must be duplicated per child. `@vitejs/plugin-react` proved unnecessary too — `esbuild.jsx: "automatic"` already supplies the runtime. The hazard the pragma introduces is that vitest's matcher is UNANCHORED, so a `.test.ts` that merely MENTIONS the phrase switches environment silently; both orphan mirrors now compute the environment a file will ACTUALLY run in using a verbatim copy of vitest's regex, watched failing on a mid-file prose mention. And the `lib/`-first RULE stays, on true grounds: a pure module is falsified by a VALUE where a component needs a render plus five mocks (CLAUDE.md, rewritten). — **A `.tsx` component has no test suite in this repo.** No vitest config runs `.test.tsx`, and `verify:slice`'s orphan guard actively flags one — so any rule living inline in a component is unguarded by construction. W10d hit this twice (the board's "finishing up…" gate, which had silently stopped agreeing with `captureAllIfReady`) and worked around it by extracting the rule to `lib/split-board.ts`. That is the right move for a money rule, but it is a workaround, not a policy. Decide: either add a jsdom project to the vitest config for component tests, or write down the rule that decision logic never lives in a `.tsx`. | T5  | low | ✅ **DONE (2026-08-29) — but only after Codex corrected my first answer, which was WRONG.** This row's harm is "a test placed there is invisible forever with no warning". I first downgraded it, arguing W8's orphan-suite guard already rejected such a file. **Codex P2 on #241 showed that was true only for the `.test` suffix** — the guard enumerated `*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx`, so a conventional `packages/db/foo.spec.ts` was neither rejected NOR executed, and the original failure mode survived intact under a different filename. Verified before accepting: `git ls-files -- '*.test.ts'` returns nothing for a `.spec.ts`, and neither vitest config includes `.spec` at any path (`apps/qr` is `**/*.test.ts`, `packages/ui` is `src/**/*.test.ts`). **Fixed** by adding `*.spec.ts` and `*.spec.tsx` to the non-running set beside `*.test.tsx`, in `ci.yml` AND its mirror in `verify-slice.mjs` — a file that can run nowhere is now rejected wherever it sits. Fixing the mirror surfaced a second defect: `find()` took ONE pattern, so the variadic call would have dropped two suffixes into the shell as nothing — a guard quietly looking for less than it claims. It is variadic now. `packages/db` and `packages/config` still define no `test` script, and that stays a design note: they host no tests, and a suite dropped there is now loudly rejected rather than silently skipped. | closed (#241, `c81283f`) | W8 spec / CI read        |
| T6  | low | ✅ **DONE (2026-08-29) — wired, and the tree was NOT clean after all.** `pnpm format:check` now runs in `ci.yml`'s fast lane beside `check:types-sorted`. This row previously said "the tree is currently clean so it would land green" — **that was already false when the step was added**: `apps/qr/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` was sitting on `main` unformatted, merged by #240, whose own round-2 rework left an import multi-line after a symbol was removed from it. Every required check on that PR was green. So the guard's justification was demonstrated by the very PR that filed it, which is the most honest argument for it available and is why the drift is recorded here rather than quietly fixed. Red-first: injected drift → `[warn] … Code style issues found`, exit 1; restored → `All matched files use Prettier code style!`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | closed                   | M70 / CI read 2026-08-25 |

### M119 — fails closed is not tells the truth (long form)

The row's Item cell (moved verbatim, 2026-10-08):

**"Fails closed" and "tells the truth" are different properties, and only the first was ever audited — SIX more sites state a cause they never established, and one skips a money guard entirely.** M116 fixed one instance; a blind sweep for the SHAPE (4 auditors over `app/api/**`, `lib/*.ts`, the authz/lock primitives and the Server Actions; every candidate then put to a refute-biased verifier against real source) returned **7 confirmed, 1 refuted** — the refuted one being `setup-intent` itself, refuted because M116 had already fixed it mid-sweep. The #226 census that cleared these asked _"does it fail closed?"_ — every one of them does. It never asked whether the SENTENCE is true, which is the question M116 was actually about. **✅ (a) DONE — `tabs.ts:66` (HIGH, FAILS OPEN), the one that was NOT a copy defect.** The `qr_carts` read's `{ error }` was discarded, so `payCart` was null, `paymentInFlightReason(null)` returns null by DELIBERATE contract (`pay-guard.ts:38`, pinned by `pay-guard.test.ts:142`) — null means "there is no cart", not "we could not tell" — and the refusal _"Someone's paying right now"_ was silently SKIPPED. A wrong OUTCOME on a money guard, not a wrong sentence. Fixed by binding the error and failing closed, which also separates the two reasons `payCart` can be null: a genuinely ABSENT cart still falls through to the RPC (authoritative on existence, answers `not_open`), only an UNREADABLE one refuses. **The fix is in the caller, not in `paymentInFlightReason`** — all NINE call sites were read and the other eight already refuse an unreadable or absent cart before calling (`floor.ts:463`, `approvals.ts`/`voids.ts` bind `cartError`; `staff-cart.ts`/`terminal.ts` via `openCartFor`'s `unavailable`/`!cart`; `approvals.ts:170` spells it `if (cart && …)`). One caller not honouring a contract is not a reason to change the contract at nine sites. `lib/tabs.test.ts` (4 cases) watched failing first — case 1 caught `res.ok === true`, the tab actually opening on an unreadable cart, and case 4 caught a quiet second symptom nobody had filed: the audit row was written with a NULL `session_id` (`payCart?.session_id ?? null`). **⚠️ And the coverage guard could not see this file at all** — `tabs.ts` matched NO `MONEY_MARKER`, so the money mutex was revertible with every gate green. `paymentInFlightReason` is now a marker (listed as a FUNCTION, like `captureAllIfReady`/`summarizeRefund` — the money lives in the decision, not a column); proven red-first. Note this brings `floor.ts`, `approvals.ts` and `voids.ts` under the marker with no mutant yet — deliberate and not silent, since the guard only demands one for a CHANGED file. **⚠️ The sweep's read of `pay-guard.ts:67` was WRONG on the remedy and is retracted here:** that `return "split_in_progress"` on a read error is a documented W10d fail-CLOSED decision, not a defect. Its only real residue is that staff see a specific sentence for an outage — a copy/granularity nit, NOT something to make fail open. Verify each remaining item the same way before acting on it. **The five fabricated diagnoses:** `create-share-intent/route.ts:51` — `{ data: share }` drops `error`, so a failed read tells a payer _"You're not part of this split."_ while the SAME handler re-reads the SAME table correctly 200 lines later (`nowErr` → 503), two standards in one file · `grocery.ts:73` (found INDEPENDENTLY by two auditors) — a dropped error makes every unreadable scan _"Not found: `<barcode>` — try searching by name"_, so a shopper is told their real product does not exist · `reorder.ts:128` — the availability read's error is dropped and `itemById` is EMPTY, so on a failed read EVERY item is reported _"isn't available today"_ · `pay-guard.ts:67` (HIGH) — the interesting variant: the error IS bound and logged, and the function returns `"split_in_progress"` **anyway**, so staff are told _"This table has a split payment in progress"_ about a table that may have none — binding an error is not the same as answering honestly with it; the outage needs its own return value, not the nearest refusal · `lock.ts:68` (MED) — a dropped error makes an unreadable status read `"closed"`, and `create-intent:51` answers _"This order is no longer open."_ The sibling read THREE LINES ABOVE binds its error (`if (error) throw error;`), directly under a comment promising to _"message it honestly"_. **Fix toward `create-intent`'s shape, which is already right:** separate _"the read failed"_ (generic, honest, 5xx) from _"the answer was X"_ (specific, true, 4xx). **Deliberately NOT fixed in the M116 PR** — that PR closes the row it was filed for; a class gets its own change so each fix can be watched failing on its own surface. Verifiers also corrected two supporting claims inside otherwise-real findings (a "no retry is offered" that `SharePay.tsx` disproves), so re-verify each before fixing rather than trusting the summary. **✅ CLOSED (2026-08-25) — (b)–(e) done, and TWO of the four were mis-filed as mere copy defects.** **(d) `grocery.ts:73` was a wrong OUTCOME, not a wrong sentence:** `unknown_barcode` sits in `grocery-queue.ts`'s `REJECT_REASONS`, so the offline queue treats it as definitive — dequeue, tell the shopper, never retry. An unreadable catalog read answering `unknown_barcode` therefore **permanently discarded a queued scan** during a reconnect drain, while the queue's own fall-through comment (`return "retry" // locked / settling / unreadable`) names the bucket it should have landed in. The fix needed nothing new: `ScanAddFailure` already includes `CartUnavailable`, whose `unreadable` variant is documented as "a failed read … the caller must offer Retry and MUST NOT offer to start a fresh basket"; `isTerminal` is false for it and the page's final `else` already renders honest transient copy. The right answer was in the codebase; the read wasn't using it. **(e) `reorder.ts:128` likewise:** an empty `itemById` does not mean nothing is available, it means we never asked — every food line was skipped as `gone`, so the reorder added ZERO dishes and made one false statement per dish. (An earlier wording said "empty cart"; Codex round 1 correctly flagged that as overstated — `reorderOrder` only inserts, never clears, so a cart that already held dishes stays non-empty. The functional claim stands, the wording did not.) **The first fix REFUSED the whole reorder and that over-blocked — also Codex round 1, also right.** `priceItem` re-reads `is_active,is_sold_out` on every add and throws, so the batch read is an optimisation plus a source of precise skip reasons, never the only thing between a diner and a delisted dish; and the refusal advertised "try again in a moment" into a screen with NO retry path (`MenuBrowser` sets `reorderRan.current = true` and strips the `reorder` URL param before calling, so the effect never re-runs). The shipped shape falls through to the per-line gate instead — which needed `priceItem`'s refusal to carry its reason (`ItemUnsellableError`), because otherwise a sold-out dish on that path came back `needs_choices`, trading a wrong outcome for a wrong sentence. Two mutants pin the two halves. **(b) `lock.ts:68`** returned `closed` on an unreadable status read, so `create-intent` told a diner whose order is open that it is "no longer open" — blocking checkout. `LockResult` gains `unavailable` → a retryable 503. **This is the SAME defect the comment one statement above already describes and fixes on the UPDATE**, where it had given EVERY checkout a spurious 409 after the PostgREST 14 upgrade; the identical shape survived three lines below. **(c) `create-share-intent:51`** denied membership on a dropped error, with a 400 (client fault) for our outage — while the same handler binds `nowErr` → 503 on the SAME table 200 lines below. All four watched failing first (`expected 'closed' not to be 'closed'`, `expected 'unknown_barcode' not to be 'unknown_barcode'`, `expected 400 to be 503`, `expected true to be false`) and pinned by four mutants (215 total). ⚠️ The reorder fixture initially passed at an EARLIER guard — the order-lookup mock lacked `earned_by`/`status`, so both cases bailed at "That order isn't available to reorder." and the defect case was red for an unrelated reason; an anti-degeneracy assert now pins that the case reaches the availability logic at all. **The through-line across (b), (c) and (e): in each file the identical shape sat immediately beside a corrected instance.** Fixing one read does not fix its neighbour, and the neighbour is where the next defect lives. **⚠️ Codex round 2 then found the fix's OWN instance of the class, and it is the sharpest one in the item.** `priceItem` read the item with `.single()`, which reports a **0-row result as an ERROR** — so `if (error  /  /  !item)`folded _"this dish is no longer in the catalog"_ together with _"we could not reach the catalog"_ and answered`gone`for both. Unreachable from`reorderOrder`while it refused outright on a failed batch read; the round-1 fallback made it reachable and put the fabricated diagnosis straight back onto the screen the fallback exists to keep honest.`.maybeSingle()` separates them (`{ data: null, error: null }`for a genuine no-row — the same reason the Stripe webhook's idempotency read uses it), leaving`error`meaning exactly one thing; a new`ItemUnreadableError`carries it and`ReorderSkipReason`gains`unreadable`. **The second half is the one worth carrying: `MenuBrowser`'s `unavailable`bucket was an EXCLUSION list** (everything that is not`needs*choices`or`grocery`), so the new reason would have landed silently in \*"isn't available today"\_ — re-fabricating the diagnosis it was added to prevent. An exclusion bucket makes every future case default to the strongest claim on the screen; it is an inclusion list now. Both halves watched failing first (`expected ItemUnsellableError … to be an instance of ItemUnreadableError`, `expected [ 'needs_choices' ] to include 'unreadable'`) and pinned by two more mutants (218 total).
